body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students add and subtract rational numbers, represent them on a horizontal or vertical number line, understand that opposites combine to 0, and find distance as the absolute value of a difference (7.NS.A.1).
- Students multiply and divide rational numbers, explain the sign rules, and convert fractions to terminating or repeating decimals (7.NS.A.2).
- Students solve real-world problems with the four operations on rational numbers (7.NS.A.3).
- Students solve multistep real-life problems with rational numbers in any form and check that answers are reasonable by estimating (7.EE.B.3).

MATERIALS
- Below Zero and Back (student overview)
- A large floor number line from -20 to 20 (masking tape)
- Two-color counters for zero pairs
- A vertical thermometer or elevation chart
- Fraction strips for the fraction-to-decimal work

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Below Zero and Back. Students walk the floor number line to model -8 + 3 and 4 - 10. Lesson: Moving on the Number Line.
Day 2: Zero pairs with counters: why does subtracting a negative add? Use the pattern 3(-2), 2(-2), 1(-2), 0(-2) to discover the sign rule for multiplying. Begin Multiplying and Dividing Signed Numbers.
Day 3: Finish Multiplying and Dividing Signed Numbers. Long division to turn 3/8 and 2/9 into decimals; sort fractions into terminating and repeating.
Day 4: Rational Numbers in the Real World. Students estimate before computing and compare estimates with answers in pairs.
Day 5: Assessment: Rational Numbers Check, without calculators. Reteach the subtraction rule in a small group with counters for students who need it.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: keep a number line on every desk, and let students draw jumps for every addition and subtraction problem.
- Support: give a sign-rule card (same signs positive, different signs negative) and ask students to say the sign before computing.
- Stretch/Extension: find two different pairs of rational numbers whose product is -3/4 and whose sum is negative; explain why the quotient of two integers is always a rational number, and why division by zero is undefined.
- Multilingual learners: pre-teach opposite, absolute value, elevation, sea level, deposit and withdrawal with a vertical number line drawing. Offer the frame "I moved ___ units ___ (left or right), so the answer is ___."

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This unit, your child is working with positive and negative numbers, including fractions and decimals. You can practice anywhere: check the weather and ask how many degrees warmer or colder it is than yesterday, or talk about money coming in and going out. Ask your child to explain why subtracting a negative number is like adding.
title: Teacher guide: Unit 4: Rational Number Operations
